question: Can locality and hierarchical compositionality provide a quantitative, cross-scale explanation of why deep networks escape high-dimensional sample complexity, how diffusion models learn and recombine structured data before memorizing it, and why task vectors can compose behaviors in pre-trained weight space?

key_findings.claim: For the shallow convolutional teacher-student model, locality rather than translation invariance controls the asymptotic learning-curve exponent.
key_findings.evidence: For a teacher constituent of filter size t and nonanalyticity alpha_t learned by a convolutional or local student of filter size s whose patches contain the teacher patches, Theorem 2.4.1 gives residual target power B(P) proportional to P^(-alpha_t/s); under the additional replica/spectral condition alpha_t <= 2(alpha_s+s), the thesis predicts the same exponent for ridgeless generalization. The exponent is independent of ambient dimension d, while shift invariance changes a prefactor; if s<t, the student cannot represent the target and the error plateaus.

key_findings.claim: Deep convolutional kernels exhibit a multiscale spectrum that is spatially adaptive, but this adaptivity does not make arbitrary global hierarchical targets efficiently learnable.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 3.3.1 partitions the NTK/RFK spectrum into L sectors supported on layer-specific receptive fields, with eigenvalues decaying as k^(-2 nu-d_eff(l)); the source-capacity and spectral-bias analyses then make the rate depend on the target's smallest supporting meta-patch. Yet Lemma 3.5.1 states that a randomly initialized infinite-width hierarchical network used as teacher cannot be learned faster than P^(-3/d_eff(L)), even by the Bayes-optimal matched kernel student.

key_findings.claim: The thesis's own kernel results are a negative control for its broader story: matched architectural hierarchy is insufficient without feature learning.
key_findings.evidence: A deep CNN kernel can prioritize localized targets while retaining global expressivity, but a globally dependent target generated by the same deep architecture remains cursed. The thesis therefore introduces the Random Hierarchy Model as a different, feature-learning setting in which deep networks build synonym-invariant latent representations and obtain polynomial rather than exponential sample complexity; that feature-learning classification study itself is explicitly outside the thesis chapters.

anchors.section: Section 1.5.1, kernel-regime limitation and RHM motivation

key_findings.claim: For the Random Hierarchy Model, Bayes-optimal denoising has a class-reconstruction phase transition while lower-level feature reconstruction remains smooth.
key_findings.evidence: Because the RHM is a regular tree PCFG, belief propagation computes exact posterior marginals when the grammar rules are known. Under the annealed mean-field approximation, the upward map has an inference transition only when s f<1: below a critical corruption level the root is recoverable, above it the root falls to random chance, while lower layers vary continuously. The numerical example uses v=32, m=8, s=2, L=10; a matched L=7 CNN trained on 300,000 RHM samples reaches 99.2% test accuracy and displays the predicted inversion of early- versus late-layer similarity curves.

anchors.section: Section 4.4 exact belief propagation and perfect-generalization assumption
Mean-field phase condition and CNN experiment

key_findings.claim: The natural-image forward-backward experiments are qualitatively consistent with the RHM phase transition and feature recombination, but they do not establish that ImageNet has the RHM's latent tree.
key_findings.evidence: Using an unconditional ImageNet-256 DDPM, the thesis observes a sharp logit-similarity drop near half the diffusion horizon while early ConvNeXt representations change more smoothly, based on standardized activations over 10,000 images; analogous curves appear for several ResNets. However, the hidden representations of classifiers are explicitly used as proxies for hierarchy, and the theoretical analysis assumes exact Bayes denoising with a known grammar, whereas the image experiment uses a learned U-Net. The Gaussian-mixture control rules out a simple bimodal account of curve crossing but not other non-tree higher-order data models.

key_findings.claim: A finite-time peak in dynamical susceptibility is the thesis's operational signature of latent hierarchy, and the RHM predicts a diverging correlation length at the class transition.
key_findings.evidence: Linearizing the mean-field BP map about its unstable fixed point yields xi proportional to |epsilon-epsilon_*|^(-nu), with nu=log(s)/log(F'_*) in Equation 82. RHM masking experiments peak near 0.3T; MDLM on WikiText-2 shows a maximum correlation span of about 7-8 tokens and a susceptibility peak near 0.6T; ImageNet iDDPMs tokenized into 7x7 CLIP ViT-B/32 patches peak near 0.6-0.7T. A Gaussian random field with algebraic spatial correlations instead produces a length scale and susceptibility increasing monotonically to T.

key_findings.claim: The proposed grammar-learning mechanism gives polynomial sample complexity by hierarchically clustering features that have statistically similar contexts.
key_findings.evidence: For the RHM, local tuples require P_1 proportional to v m, while detecting token-to-level-(ell-2) latent-tuple correlations yields P_ell=[1-m/v^(s-1)]^(-1) v m^(ell+1). Thus learning all L levels scales as m^(L+1)=m d^(log m/log s), polynomial in sequence length d=s^L. A very wide convolutional D3PM U-Net trained with feature-learning muP initialization acquires lower rules before higher rules, and k-means on empirical context vectors follows the same m^(L+1) scaling.

key_findings.claim: The natural-data local-to-global results support the ordering prediction, not the exact RHM sample-complexity law or a complete optimization theory.
key_findings.evidence: A 165M-parameter MD4 trained for one OpenWebText epoch produces longer-range token correlations as seen tokens increase, and a roughly 120M-parameter ImageNet-64 DDPM shows early ResNet-layer MMD converging before deeper-layer MMD. But the central bridge is Assumption 6.3.1—that the U-Net learns a rule exactly when the relevant empirical correlations become detectable—and the thesis explicitly says a full dynamical theory of hierarchical feature learning under gradient optimization remains missing. Natural-data metrics use pretrained LLaMA, ResNet, or CLIP representations and do not identify grammar rules directly.

key_findings.claim: Across the reported diffusion experiments, generalization precedes memorization and the onset of memorization grows approximately linearly with dataset size.
key_findings.evidence: The thesis reports tau_mem proportional to P for 0.5B-parameter iDDPMs on CIFAR-10 subsets of 2,048-16,384 images, 165M-parameter MD4 models on text8, Stable Diffusion v2.1 fine-tuned on 8,192 LAION samples, and overparameterized RHM D3PMs. On CIFAR-10, early stopping for P=16,384 yields reported FID 5.4 with 0% copies under the nearest/second-nearest distance-ratio rule; final copy rates range from 1% to 100% as P decreases. A local isotropic-kernel argument attributes the linear law at fixed low noise to eigenvalues of localized empirical-score modes scaling inversely with P, and synthetic experiments support it in lazy and feature-learning initializations.

key_findings.claim: The memorization phase diagram is compelling but its practical early-stopping prescription is not yet an externally validated, model-agnostic rule.
key_findings.evidence: Memorization is detected through validation-loss bifurcation and modality-specific copying metrics, and tau_mem is fitted over limited dataset-size ranges while architectures, training budgets, and data distributions vary across experiments. The kernel derivation assumes separated Gaussian modes at fixed low noise and an isotropic local kernel; the feature-learning result is empirical. The thesis therefore supports a time-scale hypothesis, but it does not provide a calibrated threshold that guarantees privacy, copyright safety, or absence of semantic memorization on unseen production data.

anchors.section: Copy criterion and reported copy rates

key_findings.claim: For task arithmetic, weight disentanglement is defined as the exact functional non-interference property needed for arithmetic, rather than an independently derived causal mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: Property 1 requires each task vector to change outputs only on its disjoint task support. Property 3 decomposes the edited function into support-localized components, and the thesis explicitly shows it is equivalent to Property 1. This equivalence is mathematically clean, but because task supports are assumed non-intersecting and disentanglement is defined by the desired behavior, it characterizes success rather than explaining why real pretraining produces it.

key_findings.claim: Explicit tangent-space fine-tuning improves the reported CLIP task-addition and task-negation benchmarks, even though post-hoc linearization shows that ordinary CLIP fine-tuning is not itself in the linear regime.
key_findings.evidence: Across eight vision tasks, task addition with ViT-B/32 improves from 71.4% absolute/76.5% normalized accuracy for nonlinear fine-tuning to 76.5%/85.4% for linear fine-tuning; ViT-L/14 improves from 85.1%/88.8% to 88.5%/93.5%. For task negation at 95% control-task retention, the target accuracy falls from 24.0% to 10.9% for ViT-B/32 and from 18.0% to 7.9% for ViT-L/14. Post-hoc linearized single-task predictors underperform nonlinear ones, rejecting the claim that ordinary task arithmetic simply inherits NTK linearity.

key_findings.claim: Localized NTK eigenfunctions are sufficient for task arithmetic, but their claimed empirical role is based on a small finite-support diagnostic and they are necessary only under an extra local-linear-independence condition.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 1/6 says tasks represented by eigenfunctions supported inside their respective disjoint domains do not interfere. The thesis itself notes that nonlocalized eigenfunctions may cancel outside a domain; Proposition 7 makes localization necessary only when nonzero eigenfunctions remain linearly independent on each task domain. Empirically, finite-width CLIP NTKs are estimated by SVD on 200 training points per dataset and show higher local energy on the task support; randomly initialized models show weaker localization and fail task addition, which is consistent evidence rather than a causal pretraining analysis.

key_findings.claim: The dissertation's strongest novelty is an integrated physics narrative, not a single unified theorem or a new empirical replication of every component.
key_findings.evidence: Chapters 2-8 each state that they are revised versions of previously published or submitted papers from 2021-2025. The synthesis connects local-kernel spectra, RHM diffusion, staged grammar learning, memorization time, and task-vector localization under the common language of locality and compositionality, but the mathematical objects and evidence regimes differ substantially across parts and no theorem derives task-space disentanglement from the data-space hierarchy.

method.core_idea: Treat locality and compositionality as structural reductions of effective dimension, then follow that structure from kernel spectra, through hierarchical latent variables and diffusion dynamics, to localized functional changes induced by task vectors.
method.mechanism: The thesis combines exact/asymptotic spectral analysis of infinite-width convolutional kernels; a regular-tree probabilistic context-free grammar with exact belief propagation and annealed mean-field theory; feature-learning diffusion experiments and correlation-based sample-complexity calculations; training-time memorization diagnostics and a low-noise kernel scaling ansatz; and a functional definition of weight disentanglement linked to localized NTK eigenfunctions and tangent-space fine-tuning.
assumptions: Kernel inputs and constituent kernels satisfy strong symmetry, smoothness, patch-containment, or product-sphere/torus conditions; ridgeless rates additionally use a spectral-bias/replica ansatz.
The RHM is a fixed-depth regular tree with constant branching, random unambiguous context-free rules, equal rule probabilities, and known grammar for exact denoising.
Annealed mean-field BP messages adequately represent quenched finite-tree fluctuations.
Wide muP U-Nets learn detectable context correlations and form the corresponding latent clusters under gradient-based optimization.
Classifier, CLIP, ResNet, and LLM representations are valid proxies for semantic hierarchy and coherence in natural data.
Validation-loss bifurcation and selected nearest-neighbor metrics identify practically relevant memorization.
The low-noise empirical score separates into localized modes and an isotropic kernel's expansion controls their training time.
Task supports are disjoint, task-vector coefficients remain in the tested neighborhood, and finite-support NTK localization reflects population function-space localization.

techniques.role: Separates locality from weight sharing by diagonalizing local and convolutional kernels and deriving learning-curve exponents.
Indexes deep-CNN eigenfunctions by receptive-field scale and links eigenvalue decay to effective spatial dimension.
Supplies a tractable PCFG ensemble with nested higher-order correlations and exponentially many possible strings.
Computes exact RHM posteriors and samples under forward-backward corruption when the grammar is known.
Reduces BP message evolution to a scalar map and predicts root reconstruction and critical correlation-length behavior.
Measures the volume of token or patch changes that co-vary across repeated denoising trajectories.
Explains staged latent recovery and polynomial grammar-rule sample complexity through synonym clustering.
Keeps very wide U-Nets in a feature-learning rather than lazy regime for synthetic grammar experiments.
Separates partial generalization, full generalization, and training-set reproduction by dataset size and optimization time.
Defines task arithmetic as non-interfering localized changes over disjoint input supports.
Optimizes task vectors directly in the pretrained model's linearization to increase measured disentanglement.
Uses finite-width NTK SVD to estimate whether task-relevant eigenfunctions concentrate on a task's data support.

evaluations.setting: Shallow convolutional/local kernel teacher-student regression on hypercubes, spheres, very-wide empirical NTKs, and CIFAR-10 class pairs.
evaluations.metric: Mean-squared generalization error versus number of samples and fitted power-law exponent.
evaluations.result: Synthetic learning curves follow the predicted dimension-independent alpha_t/s exponent when student patches contain teacher patches; shift invariance changes mainly the prefactor, and smaller filters improve CIFAR-10 empirical exponents.
evaluations.baseline: Matched/mismatched local, convolutional, and fully connected kernels across filter sizes and input dimensions.

evaluations.setting: Deep hierarchical NTK/RFK teacher-student regression under multiple depths, filter sizes, input normalizations, and overlapping patches.
evaluations.result: Sixteen-realization experiments support spatial adaptivity and the predicted curse for global matched hierarchical targets; noisy optimally regularized runs match the stated bound, and qualitative rates persist beyond the nonoverlap assumption.
evaluations.baseline: Shallow/deep matched and mismatched kernels, fully connected NTKs, ridgeless versus optimally regularized regression.

evaluations.setting: Forward-backward ImageNet-256 diffusion with a class-unconditional iDDPM and pretrained ConvNeXt/ResNet classifiers.
evaluations.metric: Standardized layerwise cosine similarity between original and regenerated images.
evaluations.result: Logits undergo a sharp class transition near the middle of the trajectory while early representations vary more smoothly and sometimes persist after the class changes.
evaluations.baseline: RHM belief-propagation curves, three ResNet variants, and a six-layer Gaussian-mixture classifier control.

evaluations.setting: RHM epsilon-process and masking diffusion with v=32, m=8, s=2 and depth about 9-10.
evaluations.metric: Layerwise reconstruction probability, correlation function, correlation length, and dynamical susceptibility.
evaluations.result: Exact BP simulations agree closely with the mean-field class transition; correlation length and susceptibility peak at the root transition, around epsilon=0.74 or masking time about 0.3T in the displayed settings.
evaluations.baseline: Annealed mean-field theory and a Gaussian random field with matched long-range spatial correlations.

evaluations.setting: MDLM forward-backward diffusion on WikiText-2 and iDDPM forward-backward diffusion on ImageNet.
evaluations.result: Language change correlations span about 7-8 tokens and peak near 0.6T over 300 sequences and 50 trajectories; ImageNet susceptibility peaks near 0.6-0.7T over 344 images and 128 trajectories.
evaluations.baseline: Synthetic RHM critical behavior and Gaussian-field monotone behavior.

evaluations.setting: Very-wide convolutional D3PM U-Nets trained on RHM strings across dataset sizes and synonym counts.
evaluations.metric: Per-level grammar accuracy, correlation range, latent-representation sensitivity, and threshold sample complexity.
evaluations.result: Rules and synonym invariances emerge sequentially from lower to higher levels, and measured sample complexity follows m^(L+1) for L=2 and L=3.
evaluations.baseline: Correlation-based k-means using one-token or one-tuple contexts, online versus offline training, and analytic sampling-noise thresholds.

evaluations.setting: MD4 on OpenWebText and an approximately 120M-parameter iDDPM on ImageNet-64 over training checkpoints.
evaluations.metric: Generated-token correlation/perplexity by context length and ResNet-18 layerwise MMD.
evaluations.result: Longer-range text coherence and deeper image-representation agreement appear later in training than local statistics.
evaluations.baseline: OpenWebText validation perplexity, ImageNet validation embeddings, and early versus late model checkpoints.

evaluations.setting: Overparameterized iDDPM, Stable Diffusion, MD4, and RHM D3PM training across dataset sizes.
evaluations.metric: Train/validation diffusion losses, copy rate or nearest-neighbor similarity, FID, and grammar validity.
evaluations.result: All tested settings show a generalizing interval before copying, with tau_mem approximately proportional to P; the CIFAR-10 P=16,384 early-stopped model reports FID 5.4 and 0% copies.
evaluations.baseline: Different dataset sizes, disjoint-training-set model pairs, early versus final checkpoints, and synthetic partial/full-generalization thresholds.

evaluations.setting: CLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/14 task arithmetic over eight vision tasks, plus random-initialization controls.
evaluations.metric: Absolute and normalized task-addition accuracy, target/control accuracy under task negation, and disentanglement error.
evaluations.result: Linear fine-tuning improves task addition and negation relative to nonlinear task vectors; random-initialized ViTs can learn some individual tasks but their summed task vectors remain near chance.
evaluations.baseline: Nonlinear fine-tuning, post-hoc linearization, explicit linear fine-tuning, pretrained checkpoints, and random initialization.

limitations: Author-stated: the RHM uses a fixed regular tree, constant branching, random unambiguous production rules, and no context sensitivity; natural language has irregular, ambiguous, mildly context-sensitive structure.
Author-stated: a complete gradient-dynamics theory for learning hierarchical features across network layers is absent.
Author-stated: the origin of weight disentanglement during pretraining is unknown, and the work does not identify which objectives or data properties create it.
Author-stated: kernel theory does not explain the efficient learning of global hierarchical tasks and deliberately motivates a move to feature learning.
Reviewer inference: the thesis unifies themes rhetorically, but it does not mathematically connect input locality, diffusion grammar learning, and task-vector localization in one model.
Reviewer inference: several asymptotic rates rely on replica/spectral-bias or Gaussian-universality assumptions outside the rigorous theorem conditions.
Reviewer inference: exact RHM denoising assumes the tree and all production rules are known, which is substantially stronger than a learned natural-data diffusion model.
Reviewer inference: natural-data hierarchy is inferred through pretrained representation proxies, so the results do not recover or validate an actual latent parse/tree.
Reviewer inference: the natural-language and image experiments show ordering and critical-like peaks but do not test the exact theoretical exponents or RHM sample-complexity constants.

Reviewer inference: memorization is measured with narrow duplicate criteria and limited dataset-size sweeps; semantic, prompt-conditioned, rare-example, and privacy leakage may begin on different timescales.
Reviewer inference: task-arithmetic theory assumes disjoint task domains, while real tasks and capabilities often overlap and may require shared features.
Reviewer inference: the NTK-localization diagnostic uses 200 points per dataset and finite output-logit kernels, without uncertainty or a population-level causal intervention.
Reviewer inference: nearly all substantive chapters are revised earlier papers, so the dissertation's incremental contribution is primarily synthesis and cross-part framing.
failure_modes: Teacher patches fall outside student patches or s<t, leaving target components outside the student's kernel span and a nonzero error floor.
A target depends nonlinearly on the full input, making a deep convolutional kernel's rate decay with full effective dimension despite matched hierarchy.
RHM density crosses s f>=1, so small input corruption propagates upward and root inference becomes impossible for any nonzero asymptotic noise.
A data distribution has long-range second-order correlations but no critical latent-variable transition, producing monotone rather than finite-time susceptibility growth.
A diffusion model learns local grammar constraints but lacks enough samples or optimization time for higher-level rules, yielding locally plausible and globally inconsistent outputs.
Training continues beyond the population-like score window, causing validation loss and sample diversity to deteriorate as empirical-score modes are fit.
A copy detector misses transformed, semantic, or conditioning-dependent memorization and declares an unsafe checkpoint non-memorizing.
Task vectors are added outside the small coefficient neighborhood where measured disentanglement holds, causing nonlinear cross-task interference.
Task supports overlap or share indispensable features, invalidating the disjoint-domain decomposition used by the task-arithmetic property.
A randomly initialized or insufficiently pretrained model lacks localized task structure, so individually useful fine-tuning directions collapse under vector addition.
Tangent-space fine-tuning preserves non-interference but loses too much single-task accuracy or becomes computationally impractical at larger model scale.
reusable_insights: Separate a structural prior's effect on the learning-curve exponent from its effect on finite-sample prefactors; locality and weight sharing need not play the same role.
Use a matched hierarchical kernel teacher as a negative control: architectural hierarchy alone can be expressive yet statistically unlearnable without feature adaptation.
A forward-backward corruption protocol plus layerwise or tokenwise susceptibility can probe which scales of a learned distribution change together.
Critical peaks should be compared against covariance-matched Gaussian and mixture controls so higher-order hierarchy is not confused with generic spatial correlation or multimodality.
For latent compositional data, estimate sample complexity by comparing context-correlation signal to finite-sample noise and test the implied clusters directly.
Measure local-to-global acquisition with multiple independent proxies—rule validity, representation invariance, correlation length, and held-out likelihood—not only visual quality.
Treat generalization and memorization as competing optimization timescales, and report quality, novelty, and duplicate risk throughout training rather than only at convergence.
For model merging, distinguish a functional non-interference condition from its possible causes, such as feature specialization, gradient alignment, parameter masks, or localized kernels.
When claiming eigenfunction localization, state whether it is sufficient, necessary only under extra independence assumptions, or merely an empirical finite-sample diagnostic.
A dissertation-level synthesis should explicitly label which links are proved, which are model analogies, and which are cross-domain empirical correspondences.
open_questions: Can an irregular, ambiguous, context-sensitive hierarchy retain tractable correlation and diffusion predictions while better modeling natural language and images?
What nonasymptotic optimization dynamics make deep U-Nets discover successive latent levels under SGD or Adam?
Can forward-backward susceptibility recover identifiable constituents or parses rather than only a scalar critical signature?
Do the phase transition and correlation-length exponent survive alternative noising paths, flow matching, stochastic interpolants, and modern transformer denoisers quantitatively?
Which measurable data statistics distinguish the RHM hierarchy from other higher-order non-Gaussian generative structures?
Can the polynomial grammar sample-complexity prediction be tested at scale while controlling architecture, compute, and tokenizer effects?
How universal is tau_mem proportional to P across model size, data duplication, conditioning, noise schedules, optimizers, and semantic memorization metrics?
Can early stopping deliver formal privacy or copyright-risk guarantees rather than only lower measured duplication?
What pretraining objectives, data diversity, or architectural properties produce weight disentanglement and localized task features?
How should task arithmetic be reformulated when task supports overlap and when beneficial task sharing is required?
Are task-gradient alignment, task-feature specialization, sparse parameter support, and NTK eigenfunction localization different views of one mechanism or genuinely competing mechanisms?

competitive_landscape.title: Eigenspace Restructuring: A Principle of Space and Frequency in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Xiao independently derives a space-frequency eigenspace decomposition and high-dimensional generalization theory for infinite-width deep CNNs, including curse-breaking claims. The thesis analyzes a fixed-dimension, large-sample asymptotic with receptive-field sectors and emphasizes the negative result for globally supported matched hierarchical teachers.

competitive_landscape.title: How Deep Networks Learn Sparse and Hierarchical Data: the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model
competitive_landscape.difference: The Sparse RHM adds spatial sparsity and discrete transformation invariance, quantifying how both sparsity and hierarchy affect CNN sample complexity. It directly relaxes one missing ingredient of the thesis's regular dense RHM, but still retains a synthetic hierarchical generator rather than resolving irregular or context-sensitive natural data.

competitive_landscape.title: Dynamical Regimes of Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Biroli et al. derive speciation and memorization-collapse transitions from optimally trained empirical scores in high dimension and connect them to covariance spectra and excess entropy. The thesis's RHM transition instead targets hierarchical root reconstruction, low-level feature persistence, and a finite-time susceptibility peak that Gaussian mixtures do not reproduce.

competitive_landscape.title: U-Nets as Belief Propagation: Efficient Classification, Denoising, and Diffusion in Generative Hierarchical Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Mei proves that U-Nets can implement or approximate belief-propagation denoising in tree generative models and supplies efficient sample-complexity bounds. This supports the thesis's architectural analogy, while separating representability/learnability guarantees from its empirical claim that gradient training discovers the RHM grammar level by level.

competitive_landscape.title: An Analytic Theory of Creativity in Convolutional Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Kamb and Ganguli explain combinatorial novelty through locality and equivariance preventing optimal score matching and obtain a patch-mosaic predictor with high output correlation on convolution-only denoisers. The thesis attributes local-to-global coherence to hierarchical context clustering and higher-order latent grammar, while its own early kernel chapters also identify locality as a distinct inductive bias.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Edge of Memorization in Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Buchanan et al. predict a model-size crossover between generalizing and memorizing solutions in an underparameterized laboratory. The thesis instead holds models heavily overparameterized and predicts a training-time window, with memorization onset scaling approximately linearly in dataset size; together they imply distinct capacity and optimization-time phase boundaries.

competitive_landscape.title: Localizing Task Information for Improved Model Merging and Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. find mostly non-overlapping parameter supports, introduce TALL masks, recover more than 99% of single-task accuracy from a merged vector, and identify selfish/catastrophic weights. This operationalizes localization in parameter space, whereas the thesis defines functional localization over input domains and diagnoses pretrained NTK eigenfunctions.

competitive_landscape.title: On Task Vectors and Gradients
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhou et al. prove exact one-epoch task-vector/negative-gradient equivalence and bound a second-order multi-epoch error, reframing arithmetic as approximate multitask learning. That explains how task vectors form during early fine-tuning, while the thesis's weight-disentanglement condition explains when their functional effects do not interfere; neither alone derives the other.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding and Enforcing Weight Disentanglement in Task Arithmetic
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu et al. explicitly argue that weight disentanglement describes the desired non-interfering outcome but not its underlying cause, introduce task-feature specialization as a sufficient cause, connect it to update orthogonality, and enforce it with OrthoReg. This directly sharpens the thesis's open question about the pretraining origin of disentanglement and its causal status.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Locality and compositionality form a unifying quantitative account of efficient learning from input patches through hierarchical generative rules to modular task directions in pretrained weight space.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The dissertation assembles explicit learning-curve exponents for local kernels, a negative kernel-regime result for global hierarchical targets, BP/mean-field predictions for RHM diffusion, polynomial context-clustering sample complexity, multimodal local-to-global and generalization-before-memorization experiments, and a functional/spectral theory of task arithmetic.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The synthesis is unusually broad and the cross-part negative controls are valuable, but the claimed unity is conceptual rather than deductive: the chapters use different models and nearly all are revised earlier papers. The strongest original thesis-level contribution is the explicit cascade narrative and comparison of Gaussian versus non-Gaussian hierarchical theories. Current work supports several pieces while also locating missing causes—especially feature-learning dynamics, alternative locality-based creativity, capacity-dependent memorization, and task-feature specialization behind weight disentanglement.

reviewer_notes: Read the exact cached 333-page EPFL thesis source end to end, including front matter, Chapters 1-9, Appendices A-G, bibliography, glossary, and CV. Audited every PDF page through 14 rendered contact sheets and inspected all theorem, equation, figure, image-grid, and table pages; the cache contains text for 315/333 pages, and no finding is anchored to a page flagged missing text. Quantitative claims were cross-checked against appendix settings and captions. Competitive searches covered deep convolutional kernel spectra, hierarchical/RHM and diffusion phase/memorization theories, and task arithmetic/model merging; only arXiv and official PMLR/OpenReview records were used, checked 2026-08-23. This is a primary full-text pass, not an independent secondary verification.
